subject: Priv Deploy: operator safeguard / escrow mechanism — procurement sync
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: procurement@canyonhealth.com, Anna Liu <anna.liu@canyonhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 03 Aug 2028 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Priv Deploy: operator safeguard / escrow mechanism — procurement sync

Hi Anna / team,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I wanted to put our proposed options in writing so you have something concrete for legal & procurement to review. The core ask from Canyon is reasonable — provide a defensible path for continuity if Redwood is ever unable to operate the private deployment environment. We typically approach that through one of three agreed patterns:

1) Escrow-lite (sealed snapshot + steward): Redwood delivers an encrypted snapshot of the runtime image and a sealed operator credential bundle to a neutral steward. Access is only released under tightly defined trigger events and witness procedures.

2) Witnessed transfer (forensic snapshot + on-site witness): For highly regulated instantiations, we perform a witnessed snapshot and handoff with an independent witness (tiered pricing applies).

3) Live custody with attestations (HSM/KMS-backed): Redwood retains control but provides cryptographic attestation and temporary auditor console access windows under NDA and audit terms.

Attached: proposed-operator-escrow-options.pdf and draft-orderform-redlines.docx (high level redlines we usually start with).

Questions for you so we can put a mutual action plan together:
- Which pattern is Canyon leaning to (1, 2 or 3)?
- What minimum evidence/retention period do you require post-termination (we typically propose 90 days for runbook/artifacts and 365 days for sealed-forensic artifacts)?
- Any firm audit-window constraints (e.g., max 48 hours temporary console access vs broader forensic access)?

If helpful, I can set up a 30-min legal + procurement call next week. Once we have your preference we’ll loop in Marissa and David for redline alignment.

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposed-operator-escrow-options.pdf (6 pages), draft-orderform-redlines.docx (annotated)

From: Anna Liu <anna.liu@canyonhealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, procurement@canyonhealth.com
Cc: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@canyonhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Aug 2028 09:14:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Priv Deploy: operator safeguard / escrow mechanism — procurement sync

Diego — thanks for the clear options. Canyon legal & procurement reviewed briefly and a few clarifying notes before we escalate to our legal ops team: 

- We need an example of the trigger language that would allow release from the steward in option (1). Canyon prefers objective triggers (bankruptcy, insolvency, failure to meet SLA for X days) rather than subjective language.
- Please confirm whether snapshots include full training artifacts or solely runtime images + KV cache. Our security team is sensitive to model provenance and PHI scope.
- For option (3), what level of console access do you envision for auditors? Read-only tokenized session vs full ephemeral shell? Time-box requirements are important.

I've attached an annotated copy with our first-pass redlines (canyon-annotated-redlines.docx). Procurement would also like a delta on pricing (one-time vs recurring cost) tied to each option — especially witness-based work.

Can we aim to get legal redlines back to us by EOD Wed (08/08)? That will let procurement lock timing for an Order Form sign-off the week after.

— Anna
Anna Liu
Sr. Procurement Manager | Canyon Health
Attachments: canyon-annotated-redlines.docx

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Anna Liu <anna.liu@canyonhealth.com>, procurement@canyonhealth.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 07 Aug 2028 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Priv Deploy: operator safeguard / escrow mechanism — procurement sync

Thanks Anna — that annotated doc was really helpful. Quick clarifications inline: 

- Trigger language: happy to use a three-trigger approach (insolvency/bankruptcy; failure to meet the agreed uptime SLA for 14 consecutive days despite remediation; loss of export control/compliance authorization). We’ll propose explicit thresholds in the MSA exhibit so it’s objective.
- Snapshot contents: sealed snapshot option excludes training datasets and customer PHI by default; it contains runtime images, configuration, and a minimal evidence package (forensic logs, package manifests). We can add an explicit manifest checklist to the exhibit.
- Auditor access (option 3): Redwood proposes tokenized, read-only auditor sessions (screen-recorded, time-boxed) for forensic review. For remediation or full ops hand-off we would use the steward/witness route.

Marissa / David — can you take Anna’s annotated document and draft a short MSA appendix (exhibit: Operator Continuity & Evidence) with the objective triggers and the minimal manifest list? Procurement wants pricing deltas by end of week — I’ll coordinate pricing with sales once we have the chosen option.

For scheduling: Anna — I can do 10:00am PT Thursday (08/09) or 1:00pm PT Friday (08/10) for a 30-min sync. Which works best?

Cheers,
Diego

On Mon, Aug 6, 2028 at 9:14 AM Anna Liu <anna.liu@canyonhealth.com> wrote:
> Diego — thanks for the clear options. Canyon legal & procurement reviewed briefly and a few clarifying notes before we escalate to our legal ops team: ...

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Aug 2028 10:04:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Priv Deploy: operator safeguard / escrow mechanism — procurement sync

Diego / David — thanks for the loop. I reviewed Canyon’s annotated redlines and sketched an initial exhibit draft for the Operator Continuity & Evidence (attached msa-appendix-proposed-language.txt). High level notes for negotiation: 

1) Triggers — we will take the objective-trigger approach but insist on a remediation/resubmission window prior to automatic release (proposed: 30 days cure for operational defects; insolvency/receivership remains immediate). This protects against transient outages being treated as release events.

2) Scope of sealed snapshot — recommend an explicit manifest (runtime image hash, package manifest, service config, kv-cache-not-included flag, no training data, list of third-party components and license references).

3) Evidence retention & access — propose baseline: 90-day runbook/log retention for operational artifacts; 365-day sealed forensic artifact retention. For auditor console access (option 3) we accept tokenized, read-only sessions but require all sessions to be recorded and governed by an NDA + limited to named auditor identities.

4) Pricing and procurement impact — witness-based and on-site handoffs will carry a separate SOW and one-time fee; escrow-lite has a modest one-time deposit + annual stewardship fee. I’ll work with sales to quantify.

Next steps: Diego, please share the annotated doc you sent Anna and the HubSpot deal link with procurement. David and I will prepare the exhibit redline; I suggest we propose the 30-day cure language and the manifest checklist as the first set of deliverables.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
Attachments: msa-appendix-proposed-language.txt
